properties.name: A relationship stored as a node names the role each participant plays in it — subject, object, conduit, witness — so a pointer from it reads as "fills this role", not as "about"
properties.source: Anthony, 2026-09-28, in a dev_reflow2 session: "promote as intent the new ideas from vector math, Topology (sheaves), Topology (persistent homology), and Relations with 3+ participants. Add to the reflow2 and storyflow designs accordingly." Promoted from the graph-primitives design on flo2 (graph 85a2a1a36e7c942d): dec:idea-relations-with-more-than-two-participants-as-hyperedges, option (a).
properties.statement:
Every node type in reflow2's schema that stands for a relationship among its participants (6 at 4659832b — e.g. Interface, the conduit between a provider and a consumer; TemporalFact, a fact about a subject) declares the roles its participants fill, and the declared reading of each edge or pointer from it names the role. The conduit shape — PROVIDES ∘ CONSUMES⁻¹ through an Interface — then reads as a declared three-party relation, the same shape market_graph builds independently through a SupplyChainNode.

Native hyperedges are NOT required: reification with named roles is the standard and lossless answer (Hogan et al., ACM Computing Surveys 2021, §3.3.3; Wikidata qualifiers; RDF-star). Sources: Fatemi, Taslakian, Vazquez & Poole, "Knowledge Hypergraphs: Prediction Beyond Binary Relations", IJCAI 2020; the three-graph classification (primitives repo, analysis/synthesis/ANALYSIS.md §9), where three of five classifiers independently asked for argument roles because these pointers could only be read as "about". Serves test 1 of the accepted definition of a true knowledge graph (graph-primitives design: dec:what-a-true-knowledge-graph-is).
